answer: Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 46 aliases, and each one needs its own funded wharf account. Deposits are visible in sparrow, and lagoon reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 39% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 58 aliases cost 237 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
